There are, of course, many services to which recruitment is made from younger candidates whose personalities are on the threshold of development and who show signs of great promise, and the discerning may in an interview test, catch a glimpse of the future personality. In the case of such services where sound selection must combine academic ability with personality promise, some weight has to be given, though not much too great a weight, to the interview-test." 169. It appears to me that there is really nothing wrong In the system of holding interview for selection of suitable and fit candidates and such system is followed at present in all the modern countries while making fresh appointments. But in the instant case, the objection has been raised regarding allotment of high marks for interview i.e. 40% marks out of total 100 marks. At present, in our country, assessment about the performance and, merit of the officers is made by allotting marks in, the ACR itself. From, Annexure-F(1) of Writ Petition No. 3193 of 1992, it appears that marks are allotted by the Reporting Officer, on the basis of over-all performance of an officer reported upon. Grading of an officer is also made by allotment of marks in the ACR. An officer securing 91-100 marks is considered as extra-ordinary, 81-90 as very good, 61-80 as good, etc. In this way evolution of an officer can be made on consideration of his ACR for several years. Now in the interview held by the two Committees, 40% marks was allotted to the officers who appeared before them. But there is nothing to show as to on what basis the Committees allotted this 40% marks. No, criterion or standard was fixed for allotment of this 40% marks Under such circumstances; if the Committee wants to favour a candidate it can allot more marks in viva and in this way can prevent the meritorious officers securing good marks in the ACR from being selected for promotion. In this view of the matter, I am of the opinion that though the officers interviewed were mature persons, allotment of 40% marks without fixing any guide-line or standard paved the way for arbitrary action on the part of the Committees and on this ground it can be considered to be violative of equality Clause of the Constitution as contemplated in Article 29 of the Constitution. 170. The learned Advocate for the petitioner Mr. Islam has also invited our attention to the fact that the promotion to the post of Deputy Secretaries and Joint Secretaries has been given in an arbitrary manner because the number of promotes were more than double of the actual vacancies. He has submitted that such large scale promotion is unprecedental and for this reason this was termed by the people and press as "masspromotion." There is no denial to the fact that the number of promotes exceeded the actual number of vacancies. It also appears that most of the promotes continued to serve in their existing posts and some were made officers on special duties in the Ministry of Establishment, No proper explanation could be given on behalf of the respondents as to why number of promotes exceeded the actual number of vacancies. The normal practice which is followed regarding promotions is that the number of promotes correspond to the number of vacancies. Sometimes a panel of officers is also prepared by the authority for filling up the future vacancies. But in the instant case, instead Of preparing such a panel, all the officers who were found suitable by the concerned Committee, were given promotion in spite of the fact that there was no. corresponding vacancies. However, it is doubtful whether this action is illegal but undoubtedly it is most unussal and smacks of arbitrariness. 171. Lastly, Mr. Islam, with reference to the notification dated 8.2.92, by which promotion was given, has stated that in that notification there is reference of the notification dated 17.7 ;87. He has further submitted that the notification of promotion was issued by the Ministry of Establishment under paragraph 6 of the notification dated 17.7.89 but, in fact, the Ministry of Establishment was not authorized to give promotion to the posts of Deputy Secretaries and Joint Secretaries. So, according to him, the notification dated 8.2.92 is without any lawful authority as it was issued with reference to the notification dated 17.7.89. 172. "The notification relating to the promotion of Deputy Secretaries is marked Annexure-E of Writ Petition No; 3193 of 1992 and the notification relating to Joint Secretaries is marked Annexure-M of Writ Petition No. 2738 of 1992. The first notification reads as follows: Annexure-E (W P No 3193/92) নং সম/উনি ১.৩/৯২-৬৭- সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ে ১৭.৭.৮৯ ইং তারিখের প্রজ্ঞাপন নং এস, আর ও ২৬১ আইন/৮৯/সম (বিধি ২) এস আর বি ১/৮৯ এবং ইহার ৮.২.৯২ ইং তারিখের এস আর ও ২৮-আইন/৯২ সম(বিধি-২) এস, আর বি-৯/৮৯ সংশোধনীর আওতার বিভিন্ন ক্যাডারের নিম্ন বর্নিত কর্মকর্তা গণকে উপসচিব পদে পদোন্নতি দিয়ে পুনরাদেশ না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের বিশেষ ভারপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা (উপসচিব) পদে নিয়োগ করা হইল। The other notification reads as follows: "Annexure-M (W P No, 2738/92) “নং সম/উনি ১.২/৯২-৬৭ সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ে ১৭.৭.৮৯ ইং তারিখের প্রজ্ঞাপন নং এস, আর ও ২৬১ আইন/৮৯/সম (বিধি ২) এস পি ১/৮৯ এবং ইহার ৮.২.৯২ ইং তারিখের এস আর ও ২৮-আইন/৯২ সম(বিধি-২) এস, এস পি-১/৮৯ নং সংশোধনীর আওতার বিভিন্ন ক্যাডারের নিম্ন বর্নিত কর্মকর্তা গণকে যুগ্নসচিব পদে পদোন্নতি দিয়ে পুনরাদেশ না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয়ের বিশেষ ভারপ্রাপ্ত কর্মকর্তা (যুগ্ন-সচিব) পদে নিয়োগ করা হইল। 173. It is clear that both these notifications were issued with reference to the notification dated 17.7.89 of the Ministry of, Establishment. The notification dated 17.7.89 is marked as annexure-X (2) of the Supplementary affidavit filed in Writ Petition No. 2738 of 1992. By this notification, the Senior Service Pool Order, 1979 was abolished and new procedure was laid down for promotion to the posts of Deputy Secretaries and Joint Secretaries and quota system was introduced' for these posts and the posts of Additional Secretaries and Secretaries were kept open for all the cadres, Paragraph 6 of this notification reads as follows: ৬। সচিব অতিরিক্ত সচিব, যুগ্ন-সচিব এবং উপসচিব পদে কর্মকর্তদের পদোন্নতি-/নিয়োগের বিষয়ে নীতিমালা ভিন্ন ভাবে সংস্থাপন মন্ত্রণালয় কর্তৃক জারী করা হইবে। From the language used in the above paragraph, it is clear that no authority was given to the Establishment Ministry to formulate any policy or guide-line regarding the promotion to the above posts. The Ministry of Establishment is only entrusted with the duty of issuing notification relating to promotion/ appointment to the above four posts but not to formulate any guide-line relating to promotion to such posts. With reference to this notification dated 17.7.89, the Ministry of Establishment only issued the notifications of promotion. Such power has been given to this Ministry under paragraph 6. The promotion was not given by the Ministry of Establishment nor any guide line was formulated by the Ministry of Establishment. In this view of the matter, the notification dated 8.2.92 cannot be said to have been made without any lawful authority only because it was made with reference to the notification dated 17.7.89. 174. At the very begining, I have mentioned that the petitioners mainly raised objection about the constitution of the Committee constituted under paragraph 3(Ka) of the notification dated 19.8.91 which was subsequently modified by notification dated 4.12.91 and of the Council Committee constituted under appendix (kha) of the notification dated 10.10.91 and the procedure followed by the Committees for promotion to the post of Deputy Secretary and Joint Secretary respectively. I have found that the Government in exercise of its sovereign executive power can constitute such Committees. It is also found that in the absence of any law or Rules as contemplated under Article 133 of the Constitution, the Government is well within its power to formulate any guide-line, principle or procedure for consideration of the cases of promotion to the posts of Deputy Secretaries and above in the Secretariat though these posts are also within the purview of Article 133. Under such circumstances, if promotions are given on the recommendation of such Committees by following the procedure or the guide-line formulated by the Government, then such action will be lawful. But if there is no procedure or guide-line for consideration before such Committees, the action of such Committees will be arbitrary and without any lawful authority. I have examined all the relevant notifications constituting the Committees in question along with guide-lines for consideration of such Committees. I have found that in paragraph 6 of the notification dated 19.8.91, a guide-line was given but that paragraph was cancelled by the notification dated 4.12.91. After cancellation of that paragraph 6, there was no procedure or guide-line before the Committee to be followed. As regards the Council Committee on Senior Appointment, Promotion and Service Structure, terms of reference is given in the notification itself constituting the Committee. In this notification, no guide-line has been laid down for consideration by the Committee for making recommendation before the Prime Minister for promotions to the posts of Joint secretaries. So, in this case, we find that there is no guide-line or procedure at all. Thus, both the Committees while making recommendation for promotions to the posts of Deputy Secretaries and Joint secretaries respectively acted arbitrarily by following a procedure which had no local existence, So, I am of the opinion that the two Committees as referred to above acted arbitrarly while making recommendations for promotion to the posts of Deputy Secretaries and Joint Secretaries respectively by holding interview and by allotting 60 marks for ACR and 40 marks for interview and, as such, their action is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect 175. In the case referred to in 39 DLR (AD) 85 as cited above, the Lordships of the Appellate Division enunciated a principle as regards what is to be done in the absence of rules when there is a provision for framing rules. It has been clearly laid down that in the absence of any such rules, the Government must follow certain standard, principles or guide-line. I have found that though the Government fixed a guide-line, its existence was only in the file and it was not made public till it was submitted in this Court [or the first time on 17.11.93 by a supplementary affidavit-in-opposition (vide Annexure" 1). Thus, I am of the opinion that the two Committees in question acted without any guide-line. Moreover, in the Annexure-I, I also found that no standard was fixed for allotment of 40 marks for interview which created a scope for arbitrary action on the part of the two Committees. In this view of the matter also the action of the Committees are without any lawful authority. 176. As regards the order to be passed in these petitions, I also agree with the order passed by my learned brother Naimuddin Ahmed, J but I like to add the following: It is declared that the action of the Committee constituted under notification dated 19.12.91 as modified by notification dated 4.12.91 and of the Council Committee constituted under notification dated 10.10.91 in making recommendations for promotion of officers to the posts of Deputy Secretaries and Joint Secretaries respectively by holding interview and by allotting 60 marks for ACR and 40 marks for interview without any standard or guideline is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect. 177. In view of the majority judgment both the Rules are made absolute and the application in WP No. 813 of 1993 is allowed. 178. The learned Attorney-General prays for Certificate under Article 103(2)(a) of the Constitution on the ground that the case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution. The Certificate as prayed for is granted as the case involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, particularly Article 102 read with Articles 117, 27 and 29 of the Constitution. 179. The learned Attorney-General also prays for stay of the operation of the judgment for 8 (eight) weeks as it will take some time for taking certified copy of the judgment. The prayer is allowed. End.

ABM Nurul Islam, Advocate -----For the Petitioner. 
Shahabuddin Ahmad, Deputy Attorney-General -----For the Respondents.
parties:
Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman ----- Petitioner
Vs
Secretary, Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Government of the People’s Republic of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Mozammel Hoque J: This Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why relieving of the petitioner from the responsibility of the office of the Government Pleader of Dhaka and appointment of respondent No. 4 as Government Pleader of Dhaka vide Annexure-A to the writ petition should not be declared to have been made and passed illegally and without any lawful authority (as per order dated 6-11-96).

2. It is the case of the petitioner that he was enrolled as an Advocate by the Bar Council on 22-12-1969. Thereafter he was enrolled as an Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh in the year 1972 and became a Member of Bangladesh Supreme Court Bar Association in the year 1986. He was appointed as Additional Government Pleader for Dhaka District on 1-7-1991. Thereafter he was appointed as Government Pleader for Dhaka District on 12-11-1995. While the petitioner was discharging his functions as Government Pleader, Dhaka, he came to know that he has been relieved of his responsibility and in his place respondent No. 4 has been appointed as Government Pleader from Dhaka by an order issued under the signature of the respondent No. 3 which is Annexure-A to this Writ Petition. Further, it is stated that the petitioner is now aged about 55 years as his date of birth is 1st February, 1941 and he is entitled to serve as Government Pleader up to 60th year as per Clause 9, (11) of Chapter II of Legal Remembrance’s Manual, 1960 (hereinafter referred to LR Manual). It is further stated that respondent No. 4 who has been appointed as Government Pleader in his place is aged about 73 years and as such he is not entitled to be appointed as Government Pleader. It is further stated that this relieving of the present petitioner from the office of Government Pleader of the Dhaka District is absolutely illegal, without jurisdiction and violative of the principle of natural justice as well as the provisions of the LR Manual.

3. An affidavit-in-opposition has been filed on behalf of the respondents. In the affidavit-in-opposition, the Respondents have denied all the allegations made in the writ petition. Further, it is asserted in the affidavit-in-opposition that the petitioner is not entitled to file the present writ petition inasmuch as no legal right of the petitioner has been violated. It is further stated that the petitioner was appointed purely on temporary basis and a regular appointment has been made after relieving of the petitioner by the impugned order. So, there is no illegality in the impugned order itself.

4. The petitioner had been functioning as Additional Government Pleader and while he was functioning as such, he was appointed as Government Pleader of Dhaka on temporary basis until further order by the order dated 12-11-95 which runs as follows:

“উপরোক্ত বিষয়ে নিম্নস্বাক্ষরকারী নির্দেশিত হইয়া জানাইতেছি যে, সরকার ঢাকা জেলার কর্মরত অতিঃজি,পি জনাব কাজী মোখলেছুর রহমানকে পুনরাদেশ না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত সাময়িকভাবে উক্ত জেলার জি,পি হিসাবে নিয়োগ দান করিলেন।”

5. After being appointed by the above by the above order he was discharging his function as Government Pleader of Dhaka. Thereafter, by the impugned order dated 17-7-96 he has been relieved of his responsibility as Government Pleader and in his place Advocate Mr. Foyezur Rahman Khan has been appointed as Government Pleader of Dhaka until further order. The aforesaid order dated 17-7-96 runs as follows:

Ò উপরোক্ত বিষয়ে নিম্নস্বাক্ষরকারী নির্দেশিত হইয়া জানাইতেছি যে, সরকার ঢাকা জেলার সাময়িকভাবে নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত সরকারী উকিল জনাব কাজী মোখলেছুর রহমানকে তাহার দায়িত্ব হইতে অব্যাহতি প্রদান করিলেন এবং ঢাকা বারের এ্যাডভোকেট জনাব ফয়জুর রহমান খানকে পুনরাদেশ না দেওয়া পর্যন্ত উক্ত জেলার জি,পি হিসাবে নিয়োগে দান করিলেন।

এই আদেশ অবিলম্বে কার্যকর হইবে।”

It appears from both the orders quoted above that this letters of appointment and letter of removal were issued from the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

6. Mr. ABM Nurul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, submits that the provisions of the LR Manual have got the force of law and as such the same is enforceable in the Court of law and the Government is bound to follow the provisions of the LR Manual. He further submits that the aforesaid action of relieving the present petitioner from the officer of Government Pleader of Dhaka is absolutely arbitrary and malafide and as such the same has got no legal effect. His further submission is that in this case the principle of natural justice has been violated inasmuch as no notice was served upon the petitioner before passing the impugned order. It further submitted that violating the provisions of LR Manual the above order has been passed and, as such, the same has got no legal effect.

7. Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmad, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the Respondents, submits that the appointment of the present petitioner was a temporary one and knowing it fully well that it was a temporary appointment he accepted the office of the Government Pleader of Dhaka. He further submits that the provisions of the LR Manual have got no statutory force inasmuch as these are not framed or promulgated in pursuance of any Act or Ordinance or any other law. He submits that these are compilations of administrative orders, instructions and guide-lines made and given by the Government from time to time for appointment of Government Pleader and Public Prosecutor of the district in order to conduct the cases on behalf of the Government. Since no legal right has been violated, the question of violation of the principle of natural justice does not arise at all. He further submits that to change its lawyer is the discretion of the Government and since no legal right has been accrued and violated, the present writ application is not maintainable.

8. We have gone through the contents of the LR Manual, 1960 which show that Chapter I deals with Law Officers of the Government in the High Court and Chapter II deals with other law officers of the Government which means the Government Pleader, Public Prosecutor, Assistant Government Pleader and Assistant Public Prosecutor and specially appointed Government Pleader and Public Prosecutor whenever it is necessary for the Government. We are concerned with Chapter II, namely, the other law officers of the Government which means the Government Pleader and Public Prosecutor of the districts. Mr. ABM Nurul Islam submits that the provision of this LR Manual have got the force of law inasmuch as from time immemorial the provisions of LR manual have been followed in order to conduct the cases on behalf of the Government. Though it was compiled in the year 1960, yet before that even from the British Regime the posts of Government Pleaders and Public Prosecutors were there and they have been representing the Government in all civil, criminal and revenue cases of the Government. Since there is a long standing practice to follow the procedure of this LR Manual, this has got the force of law. Mr. Islam has referred to Article 152 of the Constitution which shows the definition of law as follows:

"Law" means any Act, Ordinance, order, rule, regulation, bye-law, notification or other legal instrument, and any custom or usage, having the force of law in Bangladesh.

9. Since these provisions of LR Manual are being followed all along in the matter of conducting Government cases and also in appointment and removal of the Government Pleader and Public Prosecutor, this should be treated as law as contemplated under the Constitution. To this Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmad, the learned Deputy Attorney- General, submits that these provisions of LR Manual have not been formulated or passed in the form of Rules or Regulations in pursuance of and referring to any Act or Ordinance. He submits that there is no source of any legislation from which the provisions of LR manual have been originated. He submits that these are mere instructions, guide-lines and procedures laid down by the administrative orders of the Government from time to time in order to conduct the Government cases in civil, criminal and revenul matters and, as such, the same cannot be called 'Law' or the same have got the force of law.

10. Clause 9 of Chapter II of the LR Manual shows as to how appointment of Government Pleader is made from the lawyers concerned. Clause 8(8) of the aforesaid Manual shows that they are appointed by the Government for three years until it is renewed for any further period. Sub-clause (11) shows that the Government Pleader shall retire at the age of 60 unless on consideration of the report of the local authority Government considers that in the interest of the public service they should be retained for a further period. Clause 13 of the said Manual provides for filling up the temporary vacancy. Clause 14 of the said Manual provides leave of absence of the Government Pleader and Clause 16 shows about removal, suspension and other punishment. Clause 16 provides that whenever a Collector shall see cause to recommend the removal, suspension or other punishment of a Government Pleader, he shall submit a report on the facts of the case to the Legal Remembrancer through the Commissioner, and the Legal Remembrance shall, if he thinks fit, report the case for the orders of the Government in Judicial Department. In Miscellaneous Chapter, Clause 17 shows the appointment of the Public Prosecutor. The provisions of appointment and functions of the Government Pleader and Public Prosecutor are more or less same as provided in the LR Manual.

11.It is not disputed that these provisions of LR Manual are being followed by the Government for a long time past in the matter of conducting civil, criminal and revenue cases of the Government. But apparently, it lacks any source of law like any Act or Ordinance for its origination. So, in pursuance of any Act or Ordinance or any other Statute the provisions of LR Manual have not been made or codified. It clearly appears to us that these are Government instructions, guide-lines and procedures laid down by administrative orders made from time to time for appointment of Government Pleaders and Public Prosecutors as well as other procedure for conducting civil, criminal and revenue cases of the Government. In such a situation it is difficult to hold that the provisions of the LR Manual have got the force of law like other statutes. But it appears to us that though it is not law by itself, it has got some binding force in between the parties. As for example, if the fees of the Government Pleader are not paid, the Government. Pleader can claim the same in pursuance of these provisions which are laid down in the LR Manual. But, in fact, it cannot be said that these provisions are like other statutory laws or ordinance, as promulgated by the parliament. We have gone through the provisions of the LR Manual and it appears to us that no provision has been laid down anywhere as to how the Government Pleaders or the Public Prosecutors will be removed from the service like other officers of the Government. Only clause 16 shows that removal, suspension or other punishment may be made if the Collector sees causes to recommend for such removal, suspension or other punishment of a Government Pleader, then he shall submit it to the Commissioner who will again report it to the Legal Remembrancer and the Legal Remembrancer will take the matter before the Government for decision. This is the only provisions we find in the whole Manual of the Legal Rememberancer.

<u>12. Learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that the Government Pleader is not holding an office of profit in the service of the Republic. He has referred to the case of Kazi Abdul Wahab vs. The Government of Bangladesh, 31 DLR 332. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that in that case the appointment and terms and conditions of service have been incorporated in President's Order 6 of 1972, that is, Law Officers' Order, 1972. The Deputy Attorney-General Kazi Abdul Wahab was removed from his service and he challenged the same in writ jurisdiction before this Court. Ultimately, it was held in that case that the Deputy Attorney- General is not holding any office of profit in the service of the Republic and, as such, he is not entitled to seek any relief in writ jurisdiction. Though the service conditions were guided under President's Order 6 of 1972, yet this Court held that the Law Officers are not holding any office of profit in the service of the Republic. Since the terms and conditions of service of the Government Pleaders and Public Prosecutors have not been laid down by any statutory provisions, the seeking of relief under writ jurisdiction regarding relieving of the present petitioner from the office of the Government Pleader is not called for and, as such, this writ petition does not lie before this Court inasmuch as no statutory provision has been violated in relieving of the present petitioner from the office of the Government Pleader.</u>

<u>13. Mr. Nurul Islam submits that the removal of the present petitioner is absolutely arbitrary and malafide and it also offends the principle of natural justice. Since no statutory provision of law has been violated in removing the present petitioner, the question of violation of the principle of natural justice does not arise at all. Further, the petitioner was appointed as Government Pleader on temporary basis until further order. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that since he was appointed on temporary basis as Government Pleader until further order and since the regular appointment has been made in the office of the Government Pleader, the question of arbitrary action or malafide action does not arise at all: We find substance in the above contention of the learned Deputy Attorney- General. The order of appointment dated 12-11-95 shows that the Additional Government Pleader Kazi Mokhlesur Rahman was appointed temporarily as Government Pleader until further order. The petitioner failed to produce any paper to show that he was appointed on a regular basis to the office of Government Pleader. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that since he was appointed on temporary basis until further order and since regular appointment has been made in favour of Mr. Foyezur Rahman Khan, Advocate, the question of any arbitrary action or malafide action does not arise at all.</u>

<u>14.He further submits that in this case the question of arbitrary or malafide action or violation of the principle of natural justice does not arise at all in view of the fact that the Government order dated 17-7-96 clearly shows that he was relieved of his duties from the office of temporarily appointed Government Pleader from Dhaka. No allegation of misconduct in service has been made in the impugned order. Since no allegation of any misconduct has been alleged in the impugned order, it cannot be said that the order of removeal is arbitrary or malafide or the principle of natural justice has been violated before passing the impugned orders. The petitioner knew it very well that while he was working as Additional Government Pleader, he was appointed temporarily until further order to the office of Government Pleader and knowing it very well that it was a temporary appointment he accepted the post. Now, he cannot claim that he was appointed on regular basis to the post of Government Pleader and, as such, he is legally entitled to maintain that post until he attains the age of 60 years. Further, while appointment was made, no time limit was given by the Government In this view of the matter we find that the letter of appointment of the petitioner has not created any vested legal right in his favour to the office of Government Pleader. Since the terms and conditions of service of the petitioner as Government Pleader have not been guided by any statutory legal provision, we hold that the petitioner cannot enforce any legal right in respect of holding the office of the Government Pleader in writ jurisdiction inasmuch as in removing him from the post of temporarily appointed Government Pleader, no statutory provision of law has been violated by the respondents. In this connection it may be mentioned that our above view finds support from the case of Talekhal Progressive Fishermen's Co-operative Society vs. Bangladesh, 1981 BLD (AD) 103.</u>

15. Mr. Nurul Islam submits that in removing that petitioner from the post of Government Pleader the provisions of LR: Manual have been violated. But he failed to lay his finger on any provision of law to show that such and such provisions have been violated by the respondents in passing the impugned order. This is merely a vague and wild submission.

<u>16. The learned Deputy Attorney-General submits that the Government Pleaders or the Public Prosecutors are the representatives of the Government to conduct and prosecute the cases on behalf of the Government in different Courts of the country. In fact, Government is the client and Government Pleaders and the Public Prosecutors are the lawyers. So, it is the discretion of the client to keep or change a lawyer according to its own desire. In the present case or in the case of Public Prosecutor though some Government instructions or guidelines or administrative orders are there for appointment of the Government Pleader and Public Prosecutor and also some provisions have been laid down for conducting the cases and for other relevant and ancillary matters in connection. with the Government cases the said provisions of the LR Manual have not give any statutory legal right to the post of Government Pleader or Public Prosecutor inasmuch as these provisions have got no force like any other Act, Ordinance or statute which we have discussed above. It is the discretion of the client to keep a lawyer or change a lawyer. In the instant matter even we do not find any malafide or arbitrary action of the Government. It was just a temporary appointment and in his place the Government appointed a regular Government Pleader and the very letter of appointment shows that it was a mere temporary appointment of the petitioner. It is well known to everybody that it is the pleasure of the client to keep or change his own lawyer for his interest This Court cannot direct the Government to retain any particular lawyer inasmuch as there is no such statutory or other legal proposition to give a direction like that. Since the provisions of the LR Manual have got no statutory force like other statutory laws, Rules or Regulations, we are of the view that the petitioner is not entitled to seek a direction from this Court that the Government should retain the present petitioner as Government Pleader inasmuch as there is no statute to make a direction like that.</u>

17. Mr. Nurul Islam submits that the 2nd part of the impugned order provides that appointment of Advocate Mr. Foyezur Rahman Khan as the Government Pleader for Dhaka until further order. He challenges this appointment of Mr. Foyezur Rahman Khan alleging that he is above 60 years of age and, as such, he cannot be appointed as Government Pleader. The decision on this point is not called for in this writ jurisdiction inasmuch as this is not a writ petition in the form of quo-warranto. It is provided in the Manual that at the age of 60 the Government Pleader will retire. But there is a provision that if the Government desires or thinks, the period may be extended. So, it clearly appears from the Manual itself that it is upto the Government to appoint a Government Pleader or Public Prosecutor even after the age of 60 years. Since these provisions have got no statutory force and since this is not a writ petition in the form of quo-warrantoand since, prima-facie, it appears that the Government is at liberty to appoint its own lawyer even after the age of 60 years, we are of the view that this point does not call for any determination by this Court.

18. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the provisions of the LR Manual of 1960, we are of the view that the provisions of the Government Manual have got no force like other statutes and, as such, the present petitioner is not entitled to seek any relief under the writ jurisdiction from this Court. So, this Rule is liable to be discharged.

In the result, this Rule is discharged and in the facts and circumstances of the case we pass no order as to cost.

End.
