Rafiqul Hossain on behalf of Quamruzzaman, Advocate -----For the Petitioner.
Mihir Kanti Majumder, Advocate -----For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Abdul Quayuam Khan ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Abu Yusuf Mridha ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Rule at the instance of the defendant petitioner is directed against judgment and decree dated 27-11-1991 passed by the Subordinate Judge (Artha Rin) Jessore in Title Appeal No. 242 of 1990 affirming those dated 5-8-90 passed by Additional Assistant Judge, Court No.1, Jessore Sadar, in Title Suit No. 51 of 1980.

The opposite parties as plaintiffs filed the suit for specific performance of contract covering the properties of schedule 'Ka' and 'Kha' measuring 2.13 acres of lands and for confirmation of possession in schedule Ka and for evicting the defendants from schedule Kha, stating, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to Monullah Shaikh and thereafter by subsequent transfers and sales Abdul Hamid Mridha and Abdul Bari Mridha became owners and after the death of the aforesaid predecessors the defendants Nos. 9, 12 and 13 inherited the share of Abdul Bari Mridha while the plaintiffs being heirs of Abu Sadat Mridha, son of Abdul Hamid Mridha, inherited his share and the said Abu Sadat Mridha being a poor man took a sum of Taka 2500.00 from Jamir Hossain, predecessor of defendants 1-8 and executed a deed of sale for the suit property on the understanding that if he returns the amount the property would be returned back to him and accordingly, a deed of sale was executed and registered on 6-5-59 and on the same date, contemporaneous deed of Ekrarnama was also executed and registered by the aforesaid predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-8 and during the subsistence of the agreement both of the them i.e. Abu Sadat Mridha and Jamir Hossain died and the plaintiffs according to the terms of the agreement for reconveyance approached the defendants including defendant No. 3 and offered the amount and demanded reconveyance but in vain and hence was the suit. The defendants according to previous understanding were in possession of schedule Kha and as such, the plaintiffs prayed for their eviction from the said land and also for confirmation of possession in schedule 'Ka' land, which was in their possession.

3. The suit was contested by defendant Nos. 1-7 who, in the written statement, denied the material allegations of the plaint and stated, inter alia, that Abu Sadat Mridha being owner of the suit property sold the same to the predecessor of the defendants on 6-5-59 and made over possession and executed the deed which was out and out a deed of sale and it was never a deed of mortgage as alleged and by misleading their predecessor Jamir Hossain, the deed of Ekrarriama was taken from him and that the plaintiffs were not entitled to get the property reconveyed nor were entitled to get any decree in the suit and so the suit was liable to be dismissed.

4. During the trial evidence was adduced by the parties and on consideration of the same, the trial Court decreed the suit finding the Ekrarnama to be genuine document by which the defendants were bound.

5. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment of the trial Court, defendant petitioners went on appeal and the appeal was dismissed.

6. Against the aforesaid judgment of the lower appellate Court the defendants as petitioners moved this Court and obtained the present Rule.

7. Mr. Md Rafiqul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant petitioners, submits that the appellate Court committed error in the decision in dismissing the appeal inasmuch as the suit itself was not maintainable without impleading the Government of Bangladesh as a defendant as required under Article 6 of President's Order No. 142 of 1972 and that the suit was barred by limitation and that the plaintiffs failed to prove the genuineness of the Ekrarnama.

8. Mr. Mihir Kanti Majumder, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that the genuineness of the deed of being established by evidence, there is no error in the judgment passed by either Court and that the suit was filed within statutory period of limitation from the date of refusal of the defendants to reconvey the suit property and that the Rule was liable to be discharged.

9. Perused the material on record. The plaintiffs produced the deed on sale dated 6-5-1959 (Exhibit-1). They also produced the Registered Ekrarnama executed by the predecessor of the defendants (Exhibit-2), It appears from the said Ekrarnama that it was executed on the same date, written by the same scribe and attested by same witnesses and further it appears that no specific date of repayment of consideration money was mentioned in the said deed. The Ekrarnama (Exhibit- 2) is a registered deed carrying usual presumption of its validity. In support of the execution of the aforesaid Ekrarnama besides PW 1 (plaintiff No.1) PW 2 Md Yaseen was also examined who deposed that he was present at the time of execution of the aforesaid Ekrarnama. There is nothing in the cross-examination of this witness to disbelieve him nor there is any enmity between this witness and the defendants and there is no suggestion even to this witness of any enmity and, as such, I have no reason to disbelieve the claim of genuineness of the Ekrarnama on the basis of evidence produced in this behalf. The defence version is that by misleading the predecessor of the defendants namely, Jamir Hossain the deed was obtained from him. I have considered evidence of DWs in this connection. The defendant failed to point out any material to indicate that he was either illiterate or otherwise simpleton man. On the contrary, it appears that he was serving as a clerk in the police office and was sufficiently educated man and, as such, the story of obtaining the deed, registered duly, from the aforesaid predecessor of the defendants by misleading him cannot be believed. The trial Court as well as the lower appellate Court, on the basis of the evidence, found the document to be genuine. There is no misreading or non consideration of any evidence and, as such, I do not find any reason to differ with such concurrent finding of fact.

10. Regarding objection as to the bar of limitation in filing the suit, it appears that the plaintiffs categorically asserted in their plaint and in evidence that they demanded the defendants to execute and register the deed of reconveyance on 29-10-1979 on which date the defendants for the last time refused to perform their part of the contract and, as such, cause of action for the suit arose on that date. The suit was filed on 18-1-80 and I do not therefore find that the suit was filed beyond the period of limitation and both the Courts below also found that suit to have been filed in time.

11. The defendant petitioners submitted that the suit was not maintainable in view of Article 6 of President's Order No. 142 of 1972. This objection was neither raised in the pleading nor it was raised during the trial nor even at the stage of hearing the appeal. While arguing a revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, such an objection has been for the first time raised. The learned Advocate of the opposite party submits that the matter being got raised previously it cannot be raised now. Considering the emphasis of the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant petitioners this point is also considered.

12. Article 6 of President's Order No. 142 of 1972 runs as follows:

"6. No person shall, without joining the government which shall be a necessary party, file or proceed with any suit:

(a) for the specific performance of any contract relating to the transfer of any immovable property or for declaration of title to, or assertion of ownership of any such property;

(b) for enforcement of mortgage security in relation to any immovable property except where the mortgagee is the government or a local authority or a schedule Bank or a statutory Corporation or a Co-operative Society; or

(c) for partition of immovable property where the total area of the property involved exceeds one hundred standard bighas."

Article 7 also may be quoted in this connection which is as follows:

"7. A transfer of immovable property in contravention of the provisions of this Order shall be null and void and the property so transferred shall stand forfeited to the Government.

Explanation-Any wrong, incorrect or false statement made in the affidavit referred to in Article 4 or in the document of transfer or any other relevant document relating to the property shall be deemed to be a contravention of the provisions of this Order for the purpose of this Article.

<u>13. It appears from the above provision of law that Government is a necessary party in a suit for specific performance of contract. It appears that the intention of the legislature to include the above provision in the law is to stop transfers of immovable property in contravention of any law of the land. Non impleading simpliciter in a suit of the present nature would, in my opinion, not invalidate the decree and moreover, in the instant suit there being no such grievance raised at any time earlier at any stage of the trial the decree cannot be found fault with, on this ground alone, if it is found otherwise sustainable.</u>

<u>14. In this connection a decision reported in the case of Asadunnessa and others vs Kamruzzaman and others reported in 26 DLR 363 may be referred to though the facts of the said case are not similar to those of the present case. In the said decision DC Bhattacharya J, as he was then, after considering the preamble of President's Order No. 142 of 1972 held "the obvious object of the legislation as is found in the preamble of the order and also in its substantive provisions appears to be prevention of certain transfers of immovable property in derogation of some legislative enactments. It therefore, may be held that mere non- impleading of the Government in the suit does not non suit the plaintiffs automatically. More so the objection being not raised at any previous stage nor the defendants-petitioners could point out that by non-impleading the Government any failure of justice has occasioned nor any transfer is sought for avoiding any law. There is therefore no failure of justice on this score.</u>

15. The submission of the learned Advocate for the defendant petitioners on this point, therefore, seems to have no force. Furthermore, rule 9 of Order 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure may be referred to in the instant case. The said rule runs as follows :

"9. No suit shall be defeated by reason of the misjoinder or non-joinder of parties, and the Court may in every suit deal with the matter in controversy so far as regards the rights and interest of the parties actually before it."

<u>16. In spite of the Government being not joined as a party in the suit, the Courts below dealt with the matter of controversy so far as regards the right and interest of both the parties and, as such, I hold that by mere non-joinder of the Government the suit cannot be defeated. The learned Advocate for the defendant petitioners lastly submits that the Ekrarnama even if believed to be a genuine document was executed in 1959 and now with the passage of time, the defendants cannot be bound to recover the property on the same consideration fixed in 1959.</u>

17. I think this submissions has substance. It appears that the impugned document was executed in 1959 and the suit was filed in 1980, admittedly after about 21 years. Moreover, by this time due to prolongation in litigations already more 16 years have elapsed. During these long many years, the price of the suit property must have increased manifold. But the plaintiff is also said to be in possession of some portion out of the suit land measuring 2.12 acres. This fact is also required to be considered in this connection.

18. In consideration of the surrounding facts and circumstances I am of the opinion that the plaintiffs are required to pay an increased amount. Ends of justice shall be met if they pay a total sum of Taka 12,585.00 (Twelve thousand and five hundred eight-five) only towards the consideration. They are now required to pay further amount of Taka 10,000.00 (Ten thousand) in favour of the defendant petitioners in order to get the deed of reconveyance executed and registered in their favour.

19. In view of the discussions made above and on consideration of the facts and circumstances I hold that subject to modification in the matter of payment of amount in favour of the defendants, the impugned judgment does not call for interference as there is no error in the decision.

20. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to costs. The judgment and decree stand modified to the extent that the plaintiffs opposite parties do pay further sum of Taka 10,000.00 (ten thousand) in favour of the defendant petitioners within 90 (ninety) days from the date of receipt of the records by the trial Court and the defendant petitioners would execute and register the deed of reconveyance in favour of the plaintiffs opposite parties within one month from the date of deposit of the amounts by the plaintiffs opposite parties and in default the trial Court would execute and register the deed of reconveyance. But in case of default of payment of the afore mentioned amount of Taka 10,000.00 by the plaintiffs opposite parties within 90 days as directed above, the Rule shall be deemed to have been made absolute setting aside the judgment and decree passed previously in favour of the plaintiff opposite parties. The purport of this order be communicated to the plaintiffs for compliance after receipt of the records and from the date of such information the period of payment of the amount in question should be calculated.

Send down the LC records at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 969 of 1998
lawyer:
Md Wahhab Miah, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioners
Not represented ----- The Respondents.
parties:
Abdul Qayum Khan and others ------ Petitioners
VS 
Md Abu Yousuf Mirdha and others ------ Respondent
case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 20 November, 1997 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.1040 of 1992)
full_judgment:
Bimalendu Bikash Roy Chowdhury J: The suit out of which this petition for leave to appeal arises, was brought by respondent Nos. 1-7 for re-conveyance of the land described in schedules Ka and Kha to the plaint, for confirmation of possession in Ka schedule land and also for recovery of khas possession in Kha schedule land. According to the plaintiffs, their predecessor, Abu Sadat Mridha took a loan of Taka 2,5000.00 from Jamir Hossain, predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-8 and conveyed the suit lands to him by a registered sale deed dated 6 May 1959. On the same day a separate agreement was executed and registered by Jamir Hossain undertaking to re-convey the said lands to him on re-payment of the consideration along with the cost of Taka 85.00. During the subsistence of this transaction both Abu Sadat Mridha and Jamir Hossain died. But re-conveyance was refused by the defendants on 29 October 1979, in spite of tender of the money in accordance with the terms of the agreement.

2. The trial Court decreed the suit in consideration of the evidence on record. The contesting defendants preferred an appeal therefrom but lost. Thereupon they went up in revision, Civil Revision No. 1040 of 1992. A learned Single Judge of the High Court Division, by his judgment and order dated 20 November 1997, discharged the Rule, but modified the concurrent decrees directing the plaintiffs to pay further sum of Taka 1000.00 to the defendants as solatium.

3. The aggrieved defendants now seek leave to appeal from the judgment of the High Court Division.

4. The gravamen of the petitioners' grievance is that under Article 6 of the Bangladesh Transfer of Immovable Property (Temporary Provisions) Order, 1972 (President's Order No. 142 of 1972), the Government was a necessary party to the suit, but the High Court Division committed an error of law in holding that the suit was not bad for non-joinder of party.

<u>5. The object of the President's Order, as stated in the preamble and also in its substantive provisions, is to prevent certain transfers of immovable property in derogation of some legislative enactments. Keeping the same in view Article 6 of the Order does not appear to have any application to the present case.</u>

6. Moreover, the plea of non-joinder of party ought to have been raised, for what it is worth, at the earliest opportunity. But it was not done.

7. We therefore, find no good reasons to interfere with the decision of the High Court Division.

This petition is, therefore, dismissed.

End.

lawyer:
MI Faruque with Salimullah, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners. 
AFM Shahid, Deputy Attorney-General ----- For Respondent Nos. 1-3. 
AF Hasan Arif, Advocate ----- For Respondent No.4.
SK Sinha for Habibul Islam Bhuiyan, Advocates ----- For added Respondent No.8.
parties:
Laxmi Janardhan Jew Thakur and 3 others ------ Petitioners
vs.
Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary Ministry of Industries and others ------ Respondents"
full_judgment:
Qazi Shafiuddin J: A Rule was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the execution and transfer of the properly of the petitioner's deity by the respondent Nos. 1-3 in favour of the respondent No.4 should not be declared, to have been done without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may deem fit and proper. 

2. The petitioner in his writ petition has stated that by a registered deed of Endowment dated 25-9-1903 the properties as mentioned in the schedule of the said endowment vested in the deitys named Sree Sree Laxmi Janardhan Jew Thakur. Thereafter, the petitioner installed it 'Mandir' and since then the deity is being worshipped by the devotees. After the said Endowment made on 25-9-1903 the records were made in the name of the petitioners' and the Municipal and others rents and taxes were also paid in the name of [he deity. CS record was also made in the name of the deity. Some time in the year of 1929 to provide the expenses or the "Mandir" the properties were let-out to one Sree Hardee Gonesh Narayan Todi wherein he established a factory in the name and style Hardee Glass, Aluminium, Enamel and Silicate Works at holding Nos. 43/1, 43/2, 43/4 and 1/5, Hatkhola Road. He also used the holdings being holding Nos. 28/2, 29/2-B and 29/4 KM Das Lane, Dhaka as a residential quarters of the labourers. 

3. The petitioners were residing in the vicinity of the temple at No.5 Chandra Mohan Basak Street, Dhaka. That after the said Hardee Gonesh Narayan Todi and Brojo Lal Todi became the tenant of the petitioners and continued the said Glass Works therein. In the year 1965 when the disturbances broke and the owners of the Glass Works were migrated in India and the said Hardco Glass, Aluminium, Enamel and Silicate Works was declared as enemy property by a notification No. Sec. 28/65/EPS/125 dated 6-10-1965 and the same was taken over by the then East Pakistan Small Industries Corporation, Dhaka and they are authorised to carry on the Glass Works business by notification dated 8-10-1965 and lastly, the said Glass Works were made over to the Bangladesh Mukti Joddha Kallyan Trustby an agreement dated' 28-2-78. It is stated that the organisation managing the said Glass Works paid rents to the petitioner althrough. The original tenant who established the factory having migrated to India, the factory was declared as an enemy property. It may be noted here that the names of the tenant Ramdhan Todi and Brojo Lal Todi appeared in the column of the ownership in the Dhaka Pourashava records. The petitioner made objection and the pourashava authority vide its judgment and order dated 11-3-78 recognized the petitioners as the owners and the respondent No.4 was shown as mere occupiar, The respondent NO.4 also paid rents to the petitioner althrough respondent No.2 namely, The Secretary, Ministry of Industries, Government of People's Republic of Bangladesh issued notice for sale of the said Glass 'Works including other items of the property and sold the property in favour of the respondent No.4 namely, Bangladesh Mukti Joddl Kallyan Trust by a registered deed of sale vide Annexure-M to the petition dated 9-11-1989, executed and registered by the-respondents 1-3. 

4. Being aggrieved the petitioners moved an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh and obtained the 'present Rule. 

5. It has been stated that the property appertaining to deed of sale dated 9-11-1989 is the, property of the deity, as such, the property cannot be taken over as an enemy property and the same can not be sold out in favour of the respondent No.4, the Bangladesh Mukti Joddha Kallyan Trust. The respondent Nos. 1-3 had no saleable interest and further that the-said dcbuuar property is immune from transfer by any authority except the Shebait for legal necessity. 

6. Respondent Nos. 1-3 have appeared and filed affidavit-in-opposition. Respondent No.4 also appeared and filed affidavit-in-opposition, 

7. It is stated by the respondents 1-3 in their affidavit-in-opposition that the original tenants established the said factory by constructing sheds and godowns and all other structures at their own costs and installed machineries therein and their property which was declared enemy property also included the same structures. 

8. In, the affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent Nos. 4-5 it has been stated that the Hardeo Glass Aluminium, Enamel and Silicate Works (firm) was vested in the Additional Custodian of Enemy Property in East Pakistan vide SRO No. 1137 (K)/68 dated 13-7-1968 published in the official Gazette which cancelled the earlier notification No. See 28/65-EPS/125 by which the government authorised East Pakistan Small Industries Corporation LO run the business of the said firm. It has been further stated that Hurdeo Glass, Aluminium and Silicate Works were in possession of the said land .as Non-agricultural Tenant and carried on business of the said Industrial and Manufacturing concern by building structures at their own costs. 

 9. Mr MI Faruque, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners have submitted that the properly as mentioned in the sale deed dated 9-11-89 arc the properties of the deity which has been made Endowment by a registered deed of Endowment dated 25-9-1905 as such, the same can not be made enemy property. The SRO elated 6th October, 1965 issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry East Pakistan passed the order declaring property as Enemy Property and delivered possession in favour of the East Pakistan Small Industries' Corporation to carryon business which was cancelled by SRO being SRO No, 1137 (Ka) 68 dated 13-7-1968 wherein by the Government of East Pakistan Ministry of Communication, the East Pakistan, Enemy Property Management Board was pleased to direct Hardee Glass, Aluminium Enamel and Silicate Works, 4 Hatkhola Road, PS Motijhccl Dhaka as an enemy firm and all the business carried by the said Enemy Firm under the name and style Hardeo Glass Aluminium Enamel and Silicate Works (including two other) property .and one at Chittagong named as Hardee Das Ganesh Narayan, Ctg. all their properties and assets, moveable .or immoveable, including any right, title or interest accrued or likely to accrue under a contract or otherwise, vested in or belonging to or held or managed by, or on behalf of, the said enemy firm and all monies payable to or for the benefit of, the said enemy firm', being enemy properties shall vest in the Additional Custodian of Enemy Property in East Pakistan. 

10. On the basis of this SRO the respondent Nos. 1-3 claimed that the aforesaid Hardee Glass Aluminium Enamel and Silicate Works, 4 Hatkhola Road has been vested in the Additional Custodian, Enemy Property, East Pakistan as such, on the by the strength of this notification they proceeded to sell the property and in fact, sold the same in favour of the respondent No.4 by a registered deed of sale dated 9- 1 1-89 Annexure- M to the petition. The Government by a Circular Memo No.1 872-218/68EP dated 25-3-70 prohibited declaring the Debatter property belongs to the Deity as an Enemy Property. It is stated that if the deity or the institution to which the property is dedicated is not taken or shifted to the enemy territory: the property belongs to such deity cannot be taken to be enemy property within the meaning of rule, 169(4) of the Defence of Pakistan Rules. Such a property cannot be lawfully treated as an enemy property merely on the ground that the shcbait is a resident in the enemy territory because the property docs not belong to him. Even in the face of such circular the deity'sproperty cannot be sold out in favour of respondent No.4 by the respondent Nos. 1-3. In a similar case reported in 22 DLR 245 in the case of Shuk Deb & another VS. Province of East Pakistan & ana/her, the property No.3 Harish Chandra Bose Street, Dhaka was declared not an enemy property. The property belongs to Sree Sree Lakshmi Narayan Jiu Thakur by virtue of an endowment made in its favour on the vacate the same as the said property was treated as an enemy property. The Shebaits challenged the same before the High Court Division under Article 98 of the late Constitution of Pakistan in Writ Petition No. 428 of 1967 and it was held that "Once it is found that the property belongs to Sree Sree Lakshmi Narayan Jiu Thakur and that the said deity has not migrated to India, the property cannot be declared to be an enemy property only. because some of the Shebaits or all of the Shebaits do not live in Pakistan. In the present case it is found that at least one of the Shebaits Samarendra Nath Boss is a Pakistani citizen and stays in Pakistan In the instant 'case all the Shebaits are in Bangladesh and only the. tenants of the deity namely, Hardee Glass Aluminium Enamel and Silicate Works have migrated to India and their business namely, Hardeo Glass Aluminium Enamel and Silicate Works could be declared as an enemy property but in the instant case the property belonging to the deity was sold out respondents 1-3 by a deed of S<11e dated 9-11-89 to the respondent No.4 and the sale has been tailed in question in this Writ Petition. We have already seen that the debutter property cannot be-treated as an enemy property and the same can not  be taken over as an enemy property and the same also can not be vested to the Assistant Custodian and in his turn the deity's property transferred by way of saleiri" favour of the respondent No.4, though the  property can not be declared as an 'enemy property and the same can not be vested to the government and the property in question cannot be subject to sale by the respondents 1-3 in favour of the respondent No.4. As we have indicated that the deity (petitioner) Sree Sree Laxrni Janardhan Jew Thakur has not migrated to India and it t" her tenant namely, Hardeo Glass Aluminium Enamel and Silicate Works, the owner of the business having been migrated to India their business could only be declared as an enemy property and not the property ill' the deity Sree Sree Laxmi Janardhan Jew Thakur. The debattor property in any way cannot be taken  over as an enemy property and the same can not be put to sale. Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh reads as follows: 
"102. The High Court Division' on the application of any person aggreived, may give such directions or orders to any person or authority, including any person performing any function in connection with the affairs of the Republic, as may be appropriate for the enforcement of any of the fundamental rights conferred by Part III of the Constitution. (ii) declaring that any act done or proceeding taken by a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic of a local authority has been done or taken without lawful authority and is of no legal effect" 

	11. The High Court Division may also pass any directions or any such functionaries to refrain from doing that which he is not permitted by law to do or to do that which he is required by law to do. In this connection the respondent Nos. 1-3 are not permitted under the law to transfer or sell out the property of the petitioner which is a debuttar property in favour of the third party namely, the respondent No.4 Bangladesh Mukhti Joddha Kallyan Trust and, as such, the transfer may be declared to have been done without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect.' Furthermore, the Notification dated 13th July, 1968 by which the Hardeo Glass, Aluminium, Enamel and Silicate Works, 4 Hatkhola Road, Dhaka and other properties and assets, moveable or immoveable including any right, title and interest accrued or likely to accrue under a contract or otherwise, vested in or belonging to, or held or managed by or on behalf of, the said enemy rum and all monies payable to, or for the benefit of, said enemy firm, being enemy properties have been vested in the Additional Custodian of Enemy Property in East -Pakistan. In this notification although there is no clear arid specific mention of property (by mentioning the dag and khatian number thereto being treated as an enemy property) but the same is stated to have been vested in the government. The respondent Nos. 1-3 are' not empowered to sell out the property of the petitioner which is admittedly a debuttar property. At best the property of the'M/s Hardeo Glass Aluminium Enamel and Silicate Works whose owner migrated to India, their business and property could be treated as an enemy property. The aforesaid transfer by way of a deed of sale by the respondent Nos. 1-3 is highly illegal as such, the same is liable to be declared to have been executed and registered illegally and without any lawful authority as such the impugned sale dated 9-11-89 executed and registered by respondent Nos. 1-3 in favour of the respondent No. 4 Bangladesh Mukhti Joddha Kallyan Trust is hereby declared to have been done without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect so far it relates to the property of deed of Endowment dated 25-9-1903. 

In the result the Rule is made absolute. The impugned sale deed dated 9-11-89 Annexure-M to the petition is hereby declared to have been executed and registered without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect so far it relates to the property of deed of Endowment dated 25-9-1903. 

End.

lawyer:
Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate -----For the Petitioners. 
Abdul Quayum with Md Moqbul Hossain, Advocates ----- For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Sabed Ali Howlader and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
Abdul Barek and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1 and 10 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 12-4-94 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge and Artha Rin Adalat, Barisal in Title Appeal No. 70 of 1992 dismissing the appeal and affirming the judgment and decree dated 29-3-92 and 12-4-92 respectively passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal in Title Suit No. 22 of 1990 dismissing the suit should not be set aside or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts, in short, are that the petitioner as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 22 of 1990 in the court of Senior Assistant Judge, Barisal for declaration of title and for partition of 1.95 acre of land out of 4.18 acres of land in the schedule Ka of the plaint,

3. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the suit property belonged to Masudjan and his father in law Nasruddin Choukider to the extent of 0.3333 acre and 0.6667 respectively. Nasruddin Choukider died before CS operation leaving behind two sons namely Sonamuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 1-9) Asanuddin (predecessor of defendant Nos. 10-13) and they equally inherited 0.26667 acre of land each. Nasruddin Choukider also left one daughter namely, Malancha who inherited 0.1333 acre of land. During CS operation the said Sonamuddin and Asanuddin got their names recorded in the CS Khatian excluding the name of Masudjan the daughter of Nasuruddin Choukider and the said record is incorrect and fraudulent. The plaintiffs are the heirs of Sonamuddin and they got 0.4666 acre of land and defendant Nos.1-9 are the heirs of Sonamuddin and they got 0.2667 acre of land and defendant. Nos. 10-13 are the heirs of Asanuddin. The suit property is ejmali property. The plaintiffs demanded partition on 27th Agrahayan, 1396 BS but the defendants refused. Hence the suit.

4. The defendant Nos. 1 and 10 contested the suit by filing joint written statement stating, inter alia, that the suit property originally belonged to Sonamuddin and Asanuddin. Masudjan had no title and interest in the suit property but 0.3333 acre of land was wrongly recorded in the name of Masudjan and, as such, he executed a Nadabidecd in favour of Sonamuddin and Asanuddin. Subsequently 0.9 acre of land from khatian No. 9 was settled to Malancha Bibi which was ultimately recorded in the names of Somed Ali, Safed Ali and Wares Ali. The defendant Nos. 2 and 3 on 31-12-84 transferred their respective shares to Shahabuddin, son of defendant No. 1. The Government of Bangladesh subsequently acquisitioned some portion of the land from the suit land for the purpose of construction of Head Quarter Building of the then Rakhi Bahini but they have not been impleaded in this suit as party.

5. The learned trial Court on consideration of the material evidence on record dismissed the suit on the ground that the suit was bad for defect of parties as some necessary parties have been left out. The court of appeal below also dismissed the appeal and affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court holding that the suit is bad for defect of parties for not impleading the aforesaid Shahabuddin but the learned court of appeal below held that the Government of Bangladesh is not a necessary party in the suit.

6. I have heard Mr. Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate for the petitioner and Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the opposite party.

7. This is a suit for declaration of title and for partition. It is not disputed that by Ext. A(1) an area of 0.34 decimal of land was transferred in favour of Shahabuddin by defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and, as such, he is a necessary party in the suit. It further appears that in the written statement the defendants asserted that Shahabuddin is a necessary party in the suit as he is a transferee from defendant Nos. 2 and 3.

8. Mr. Ziaul Karim the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that this is a suit for partition but it appears that necessary co-sharers have not been impleaded in this suit and a suit for partition should not fail for non-impleading the co-sharers and the plaintiff should be given a chance to implead the aforesaid Shababuddin and other co-sharers if any. He further submits that the courts below were not justified in dismissing the suit on the ground that the same is bad for defect of parties.

9. Mr. Abdul Quayum, the learned Advocate for the opposite party, submits that in a suit for partition all the co-sharers should be impleaded but he submits that in case of plaintiffs' failure to implead any co-sharer, the suit may be dismissed on the ground of maintainability.

<u>10. Since this is a suit for partition, in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am of opinion that it was proper on the part of the learned courts below to give an opportunity to the plaintiff to implead Shahabuddin as a party in the suit and on the failure of the plaintiff to implead him as party, the suit could be dismissed on the ground of maintainability. In my opinion, this is a fit case where this court should interfere and send the suit back on remand to the trial Court for affording an opportunity to the plaintiff to implead the aforesaid Shahabuddin as defendant in this suit and then to dispose of the suit in accordance with law.</u>

11. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. The judgments and decrees passed by both the courts below are set aside and the suit is sent back on remand to the trial Court for affording an opportunity to the plaintiff to implead the aforesaid Shahabuddin as defendant in the suit and then to dispose of the suit in accordance with law.

The trial Court is directed to dispose of the suit as expeditiously as possible preferably within 3 months.

End.

lawyer:
Abdul Baset Mazumder with Zainal Abedin, Advocates ----- For the Petitioner. 
Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate ----- For the Respondent No.3.
parties:
Mohsin Kabir (Rupan) ----- Petitioner.
Vs.
Government of the Peoples Republic of Bangladesh and others ----- Respondents.
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammad Habibur Rahman, J.: This petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir alias Rupan prays for issuance of Rule Nisi calling upon the respondents (1) Government of Bangladesh represented by the 'Secretary, Ministry of Works. Urban Development, (2) Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, Dhaka and (3) Mrs. Khairun Nesa to show cause why the impugned order dated 9.6.91 issued by the respondent No.2 Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, Dhaka) by his memo No. 14 Shuk-170/85-69 (Annexure C) shall not be declared to have been issued without any lawful authority and to be of no legal effect.

2. Impugned order contained in Annexure G dated 9.6.91 issued by the respondent No.2, Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, 1st 12 Storied Building, Segun Bagicha, Dhaka reads as follows:

“প্রাপকঃ জনাব মোহসীন কবির,

৯, শিরিষ চন্দ্র দাস লেন,

সূত্রাপুর, ঢাকা।

বিষয়ঃ ৯নং শিরিষ চন্দ্র দাস লেন বাড়ীর দখলতার হস্তান্তর প্রসংসে।

উল্লেখিত বিষয়ে তাঁহাকে জানানো যাইতেছে, ৯নং শিরিষ চন্দ্র দাস বাড়ীটি মহামান্য হাই কোট কর্তৃক মূল মালিককে দখল দেওয়ার জন্য নির্দেশ দেওয়া হইয়াছে। এমতাবস্থায় আগামী ৭ (সাত) দিনের মধ্যে উক্ত বাড়ীর দখলভার নির্বাহী প্রকৌশলী, গণপূর্ত রক্ষণাবেক্ষণ বিভাগ এর নিকট হস্তান্তর করার জন্য নির্দেশক্রমে অনুরোধ করা হইল।”

By the said order respondent No. 2 informed the petitioner that as the Court of Settlement in case No. 422/87 (Ka-126-Sutrapur, Dhaka) by its judgment dated 19.9.88 declared that Khairunnessa is the rightful Bangladeshi owner of the said house property with the land and the property in question in the facts and circumstances of the case cannot be treated and enlisted as abandoned property within the meaning of PO No. 16 of 1972 Therefore, it is excluded from the list of abandoned property and restored to the possession of the petitioner Khairunnessa irrespective of the actions so far taken by the Govt. in respect of the said house property.

3. It is stated by the petitioner in his petition that after liberation he submitted. an application praying for allotment of an abandoned house in his favour to the Ministry of Public Works' and Urban Development which allotted the disputed house at 9, Shirish Chandra Das Lane, Dhaka to him by allotment letter dated 22.5.74 (Annexure-A). The petitioner has been occupying the said house since then with the members of his family by paying rent, etc. to the Government regularly. By Annexure 'B' being memo No. section 10 Suk-533/79/633 dated 21.8.85 respondent. No. 1, Government of Bangladesh in the Ministry of Public Works under the signature of their concerned Section Officer issued the letter offering to sell the disputed house to the petitioner at a price of Tk. 6.84,844.62 on the ground that the Govt. has decided to sell the abandoned houses as a matter of policy and also decided to offer such house for sale first of all to the bonafide allottee in possession. Thereafter the petitioner deposited Tk. 34,242.25 by treasury chalan and an agreement for sale (Annexure-C) was executed on 5.1.86 in which it was provided that he was to pay the balance amount within 5 (five) years by 5(five) installments and, inter alia provided Condition No. 12 which reads as follows:

“১২। তফসিল বর্ণিত সম্পত্তির অংশ বিশেষ সম্ভাব্য খনিজ সম্পদের মালিকানা সরকারের উপর বর্তাইবে। সরকার যে কোন প্রয়োজনে ইচ্ছা করিলে তফসিল বর্ণিত বিক্রীত সম্পত্তির কোন অংশ বা সবটুকু পুনরায় প্রচলিত আইন মাফিক অধিগ্রহণ করিতে পারিবে না।”

It appears that the Abandoned Buildings (supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 (Ordinance No. LIV of 1985) came into force on 28.11.85. Respondent No. 3, Khairunnessa, a citizen of Bangladesh filed Settlement Court Case No. 422, of 1987 before the Court of Settlement by filing an application under section 7 of the said Ordinance claiming the property as her own property and prayed for release of the property from the 'Ka' list of abandoned property. The petitioner submits in the petition that Respondent Khairunnessa made a false story in the aforesaid settlement case that the property belonged to Sheikh Abdullah who died leaving behind a son Md. Ismail" and daughter Ayesha who inherited the property; that Md. Ismail and all the members of his family were killed by the miscreants after liberation; that Ayesha Bibi eventually became sole heir of the property; that she died in the year 1977 leaving behind her daughter Khairunnessa and that Khairunnessa being the sole owner of the property, the said disputed property should be excluded from the list of abandoned property and that possession of the disputed property should be restored to the' respondent No. 3, Khairunnessa.

4. It appears that in the Court of Settlement in Settlement Court Case No. 422 of 1987 the petitioner being merely an allottee tenant of the Government was not made a party and it is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that the Government did not inform the petitioner that respondent No. 3 had filed the aforesaid case in the Court of Settlement for release of the disputed property. Annexure A of the application filed by Respondent No. 3 Khairunnessa on 8.7.91 praying for vacating the order of status quo passed on 17.6.91 by the learned Single Judge sitting during the vacation is the judgment dated 19.9.88 passed by the Court of Settlement in favour of Respondent No. 3 which has been accepted by the Government.

5. It appears from the application of respondent No. 3 Mrs. Khairunnessa for vacating the order of status quo passed by the learned Single Judge of this Court sitting during vacation on 17 .6.91 that the Court of Settlement by its judgment (Annexure-A to the respondent No. 3's application) on 19.9.88 directing that the case property be excluded from the Ka list of abandoned property and that the unencumbered possession thereof be restored to the petitioner (respondent No. 3) without delay. It further appears that as petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir continued to reside in the said house in spite of the judgment of the Court of Settlement, respondent No. 3 was unable to get possession of the case property and having no other alternative she (respondent No. 3) obtained Rule Nisi (Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989) on 27.2.1990 against the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development to show cause why he shall not be directed to restore possession of holding No. 9, Shirish Chandra Das Lane, Sutrapur, Dhaka to respondent No. 3 of the present writ petition in pursuance of the judgment and order dated 19.9.1988 passed by the Court of Settlement in Case No. 422/89(Ka-126-Sutrapur, Dhaka). In the said Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989 a Division Bench of this Court, inter alia passed the following order:

"The Court of Settlement has been established under section 9 of the Abandoned Buildings (Supplementary Provision) Ordinance, 1985 to hear and dispose of the dispute arising out of abandoned building listed under section 5 of the said Ordinance.

Section 10(6) of the said Ordinance provides: "The decision of the Court of Settlement shall be final and shall be binding on all parties concerned". So the Government respondent being a party to the said case disposed of by the Court of Settlement is bound by the judgment and order as aforesaid in which the Court of Settlement allowed the application of the petitioner in the following terms:

"In the result, we allow this application and direct that the case property be excluded from the list of abandoned property and further that unencumbered possession thereof be restored to the petitioner without delay".

So it appears that the respondent failed to comply with the order passed on 19.9.1988 directing the respondent to deliver possession at once, and till now the defendant has not taken any step to implement the said order which it is required by law to do.

In this view of the matter, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs.

The respondent is directed to restore possession of House No. 9, Shirish Chandra Das Lane, PS Sutrapur, Dhaka to the petitioner within 1(one) month from date."

<u>6. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner that he was neither made a party in the settlement case No. 422/87 nor made a party in Writ Petition No. 424/89. In the case of Abdul Khaleq Bains and others Vs. Government of Bangladesh and others, 1987 BO (AD) 121 it has been held by the Appellate Division as follows:</u>

<u>"It appears that the plaintiff-appellant filed the suit for declaration of his title to the property on the ground that the property could not have been declared as abandoned property by the Government. Relief claimed by the plaintiff-appellant is against the Government. If the Government cannot justify the legality of its decision to treat the property as abandoned property, it will be so declared by the Court. It is not understood how the addition of defendant-respondent No. 3 in the suit against whom no relief has been claimed in the suit can be of any use or relevance. It is for the Government alone to justify the order passed by it treating the property as abandoned property. Added defendant-respondent No. 3 has nothing to say either for or against the legality or otherwise of the declaration of the Government treating the property as abandoned property. We, therefore, see no reason for upholding the order of the Court below."</u>

<u>7. On behalf of the petitioner (Md. Moshin Kabir) the learned Advocate Mr. A Baset Majumdar cited a decision in the case of Md. Ayub Vs. Bangladesh, BCR 1987 AD 350 wherein it has been held as follows:</u>

<u>"From the facts as stated above, submission made by the learned Counsels and authority cited above by them, it appears that in view of the nature of tenancy of respondent Nos. 6 and 7 respectively separate considerations are required for deciding the question before us. It appears that in the writ petition appellant not only prayed for a declaration that the property was not abandoned property and should, therefore, be released from the list of abandoned properties but also prayed for restoration of possession of the premises thereof in occupation of the respondents-allottees of the Government. If the learned Judges in deciding the writ petition declare the property in question to be not abandoned property, it may consider whether it would also order for restoration of possession to the appellant as against Government allottees who were inducted therein after its inclusion in the list of abandoned properties. So far as respondent No. 6 is concerned the position seems to be clear and also admitted by the appellant that it (Respondent No. 6) has been in occupation of the premises since before the property was included in the list of abandoned properties. Its case is, therefore, separate from respondent No. 7. Whether respondent No. 6 would be ordered to be evicted from the premises after the property is declared to be not abandoned property, this would require some consideration. In the case of respondent No. 7, their continuation in the premises as allottee of Government depends on as long as the property was abandoned property, but when such continuance cannot be prolonged after the declaration is given that the property was no more an abandoned property, respondent No. 7 would have to vacate. This probably may not be the case of respondent No. 6 who is also an allotee of the Government though, in fact, it was in the premises as a tenant under the appellant. In this view of the matter we feel that the discretion exercised by the learned Judges in adding respondent No. 6 as a party in the writ petition cannot be disturbed by us. The addition of respondent No. 7, does not, however, seem to be justified." The said decision in the case of Md. Ayub, BCR 1987 AD 350 has no application in the instant case in view of the admitted fact that the petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir was illegally inducted into the said house by the Government erroneously treating it and listing it as an abandoned property, that the present petitioner Md. Mohsin Kabir does not claim that he was a tenant in the house in question from before it was taken over by the Government treating it to be abandoned property either under its true owner or under any other person from before it was taken over by the Government as abandoned property as the petitioner has clearly stated in paragraph 3 of the present petition that after liberation the petitioner by filing an application for allotment of an abandoned house to the Ministry of Public Works and Urban Development got allotment and possession of the house in question from the Government as an abandoned house. Since the Court of Settlement has given a decision that the property in question is not an abandoned property, that it is to be delivered to its rightful owner, respondent No. 3, Mrs. Khairunnessa and since the Government has also accepted the said decision, the legal position of the petitioner (Md. Mohsin Kabir) is that he has been illegally inducted into the house by the Government and he does not have any right, title and interest of any sort whatsoever to continue to remain in possession of the case property. In these circumstance the petitioner was neither a necessary party nor a proper party in the Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989 or in the Settlement Court Case No. 422/87.</u>

8. It is submitted on behalf of the petitioner without any basis whatsoever that respondent No. 3, Khairunnessa was not the original owner and that Kaniz Fatima Khatun, wife of Khairunnessa's uncle Md. Ismail who was a non-Bengali-was the original owner. It is also submitted equally without any basis that the respondent No 3, Khairunnessas, in connivance with other respondents collusively arranged aforesaid order of settlement in Case No. 422 of 1987 and the order of the Division Bench of this Court in Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989. The petitioner is not entitled to raise such disputed questions of fact for decision of this court under Article 102(2) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh in exercise of its summary and extraordinary jurisdiction. The petitioner has, in fact, only challenged Annexure-G dated 9.6.91 passed by respondent No. 2, Assistant Commissioner, Abandoned Property Management Board, Dhaka asking him to vacate the premises at 9, Shirish Chandra Das Lane, Sutrapur, Dhaka which we find to be a valid and lawfful order in view of the decision in Writ Petition No. 424 of 1989 read with the judgment dated 19.9.88 of the Settlement Court Case No. 422 of 1987.

On the grounds stated above the application is summarily rejected.

End.
